violated_contract: A test that bounds a contract's duration must measure from the instant that contract's window opens. A wall-clock bound anchored earlier — at request start — charges the harness's own scheduling delay against a deadline the implementation already enforces absolutely. That delay is unbounded on a loaded runner: the event loop only observes a short handler budget when it next runs, so a correct implementation fails on a busy machine and the shard goes red for a reason the contract does not cover. test_sequenced_cleanup_waits_share_one_deadline measured 1.103s against its 0.75s request-start bound on the 2026-11-16 nightly while the cleanup tail from the shared post-budget deadline was still exactly one cleanup window.
canonical_prevention: Anchor the assertion at the absolute deadline the implementation publishes (here the deferral's post-budget deadline) and observe where the bounded wait actually lands, so the bound is independent of pre-window scheduling delay. Keep a generous total-elapsed hang guard, and prove the named regressions still fail: a wait that takes a fresh window from its own start must land a full window later, and a first wait that takes a fresh window must still be cut and recorded.
